title: Change the telescope eyepiece
hook: Change eyepiece focal length and predict angular magnification magnitude.
misconception: angular magnification magnitude doubles when eyepiece focal length doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply magnification magnitude = f_objective/f_eyepiece to compare angular magnification magnitude when eyepiece focal length changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal astronomical telescope with fixed objective focal length, magnification magnitude = f_objective/f_eyepiece. When eyepiece focal length doubles, angular magnification magnitude becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model magnification magnitude = f_objective/f_eyepiece; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal astronomical telescope with fixed objective focal length, with a nonzero initial result. If eyepiece focal length triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on angular magnification magnitude?
recall.why: Apply magnification magnitude = f_objective/f_eyepiece under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
